subject: Simplify hosted API & console language for cross-border transfers and partner terms
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Simplify hosted API & console language for cross-border transfers and partner terms

Hey team —

Quick initiative ask: Legal has asked us to produce consumer-facing language for the Hosted API privacy/terms surfaces and the Console (billing / model selection / settings) that explains how data moves, who we rely on (partners/subprocessors), and what protections we have for cross-border transfers. The goal is plain, product-facing copy — not a legal substitute — that helps customers and prospects (esp. procurement/security reviewers) quickly understand risk and next steps.

What I put together (attached): redline_dpa_terms_v1.docx and a first-pass console_helptext_draft.md. Two requests:

1) Legal review: can we avoid swapping out every legal term in the DPA? My thought: use plain-language UI strings and keep the DPA legal terms unchanged, with a short parenthetical or tooltip linking the two. For example: UI: “We may engage service partners to help process your requests.” Tooltip/DPA link: “Service partners (subprocessors) — see full list and legal definitions.” Is that ok?

2) Product/UX constraints: Laura — can you propose short copy snippets (one-liners, 1–2 sentence tooltips) that fit existing UI widths? I added a few placeholders but they need tightening. Also call out where we should show the subprocessor list link (settings vs. DPA modal).

Timing: I’d like a combined draft for external review by the Acme Health security team by EOD Wed 4/14.

Thanks —
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Product Marketing, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
attachments: redline_dpa_terms_v1.docx (docx, 45KB); console_helptext_draft.md (markdown, 6KB)
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Simplify hosted API & console language for cross-border transfers and partner terms

Steph —

Thanks for the brief. I pulled together UI-sized snippets and placement recommendations (attached ui_snippets_v1.txt). Key suggestions below — aimed to be approachable for procurement/security reviewers but short enough for tooltips/rows in the Console: 

1) Settings > Data handling summary (single-line, shown under Account > Security):
"We may route requests across regions to serve you. We protect data with standard contracts and technical safeguards — see details and controls."

2) Model selection prompt (one-line hint):
"Choose a region to keep data in that location (where available)."

3) Subprocessor disclosure (compact row near DPA link):
"We use trusted service partners to operate the platform. View full partners list and roles."

Placement notes: 1) Show the subprocessor list link in the Security settings page and in the DPA modal (two entry points). 2) For external-facing pages (pricing / docs), use the short sentence from #1 and link to the DPA and the partners list.

I kept language deliberately loose — avoided replacing the legal term "subprocessor" in the DPA but replaced it in the UI with "service partners" and added a parenthetical on first-view where the DPA is shown.

Attached: ui_snippets_v1.txt contains the variants (short/medium/long) and estimated char counts for our current UI columns.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Product Writer, Redwood Inference
attachments: ui_snippets_v1.txt (text, 2KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-13T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Simplify hosted API & console language for cross-border transfers and partner terms

Thanks for the drafts — good direction. A few legal redlines and recommendations (high-level):

- We should not remove or replace legal terms inside the DPA text. Consumer-facing UI can use plain wording, but the DPA must keep "subprocessor", "data transfer", and references to SCCs/transfer mechanisms.
- Recommended mapping in UI (first-use parenthetical):
  * UI: "service partners (subprocessors)" — parenthetical appears on first display in Settings/DPA modal only.
  * After the first appearance, shorten to "service partners."
- Data transfer one-liner for Procurement/Legal reviewers (must include method):
  "We transfer data across regions as needed; transfers are governed by standard contractual clauses and implemented technical safeguards. Contact security@redwoodinference.com for complete transfer details and the subprocessor list."
- We should provide a permanent link to the live subprocessor list in the Console (Settings > Security) and in the DPA modal. That list must be the single source of truth and updated on each onboarding cycle.

Attached: legal_redlines_dpa.docx — I added inline comments where the UI copy should link back to the DPA and suggested a short procurement-ready sentence for contracting teams.

Caveat: The short sentence above is fine for product screens, but procurement/prospects may request more detail (SCCs, adequacy, EU-US frameworks). We'll need an FAQ doc with the exact language for sales to hand to customers who ask for transfer mechanics.

Kimberly Park
Counsel, Privacy & Security, Redwood Inference
attachments: legal_redlines_dpa.docx (docx, 28KB)

Thanks for sharing the drafts and thanks to your team for the concise UI options. A couple quick asks from Acme Health security/procurement so we can close the procurement questionnaire:

1) Can you confirm the exact one-line we should include in our procurement summary? (we prefer a single sentence that we can paste into our risk register)

2) Please share the live subprocessor list link and the cadence for updates. If you could also confirm whether any subprocessors process data in jurisdictions outside the EU/US, that will help speed our review.

If you can send those two items today we should be able to finish our review and move to a quick procurement kickoff next week.
